assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Debt fell from Rp360.14bn at end-2025 to Rp257.83bn at 30-Sep-2026 [S0]. The FY2026 entry carries that nine-month repayment to the reporting date and assumes the fourth quarter is flat, so the model's FY2026 debt matches the September balance rather than assuming a second Rp100bn paydown; FY2027 carries a further Rp20bn, then flat as capex and dividends absorb free cash flow.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Engine default zero: no recurring non-operating income or charge is disclosed for FY2025 [S4].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(minority, np))

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: FY2025 paid Rp39.99bn, DPS Rp6.97, equal to 25.1% of Rp159.3bn net profit [S11]; the 25% payout is held across the forecast rather than the engine's 15% default.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Engine default zero: no issuance or buyback is planned and the 5,737.85m shares are unchanged in the FY2025 LK [F6].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House old-currency terminal growth: 4% nominal IDR, below the 7.45% IDR risk-free rate and above the macro deck's 2.5% long-run IDR inflation, so terminal value assumes no perpetual real premium on top of volume growth.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue (cash)
assumptions.basis: Cash-only SG&A ratio: the earlier 9.0% was total SG&A over revenue and still contained the fixed-asset depreciation that the da_unit line already carries, so forecast EBIT/EBITDA double-counted it. FY2025 total opex was Rp52.89bn [S0], of which the G&A depreciation share was Rp4.36bn (total depreciation Rp16.02bn [F5] less the Rp11.66bn charged to cost of sales [F50], fact F67), leaving about Rp48.53bn of cash opex, or 6.12% of Rp792.72bn revenue [F20]. The 9M-2026 run-rate is higher: total opex of Rp52.63bn (H1 Rp81.41bn less the Q3 credit of Rp28.78bn [S0]) less the G&A depreciation share of Rp4.36bn removed on the FY2025 split gives about Rp48.3bn on Rp566.1bn revenue, or about 8.5%, and the Q3 line is a derived residual rather than an LK split [S0, S15]. We hold the 8.5% cash ratio flat, above the FY2025 like-for-like cash ratio, so the base is not flattered by the correction.

challenges.challenge: The update says "We keep the rating, the target and the scenario probabilities unchanged", but the engine's target is Rp4,113.41 and TR -48.64% at Rp8,025, while the prior published model (history/v1/model.json) has Rp4,255.67 and -48.94% at Rp8,350. The drift is mechanical - the konglo lens prices off the current share price, so the lower price lowers the target - and is not the 2 Nov event. The report never names the price input or reconciles the two publications, so a reader is told the target is unchanged when it is 3.4% lower. This is the pre-existing issue the desk flagged.
challenges.answer: Corrected the 'target unchanged' claim. The Investment summary now states the current target against the prior published target, explains that the price input moved from the prior data pack's price to the current price and that the konglo lens scales with it, and that the model corrections below partly offset it by lifting fundamental value. Rating, method weights and regime probabilities are unchanged.

challenges.challenge: The cross-check metrics are FY2025A, not LTM. EV/EBITDA uses FY2025A EBITDA Rp339.4bn and P/E uses FY2025A NP Rp159.3bn, while the pack's LTM (2025Q4 + 2026Q1-Q3) is EBITDA Rp261.1bn and NP Rp193.3bn. The report calls FY2025A "the LTM EBITDA" and explains the DCF-multiple gap as multiples on "today's LTM earnings, which the 2026 cost reset has depressed". FY2025A is the highest of the last three years (FY2024 EBITDA 246.1, FY2023 184.4), not a low, and using it makes the cross-checks higher, not lower, than an LTM basis. The explanation is backwards.
challenges.answer: Cross-checks are now explicitly labelled FY2025A, the last audited year, not LTM, and the report says why the pack's LTM is not used after the revenue restatement. The DCF-to-multiple gap is explained as a horizon difference: the DCF carries 63.7% of its value in the extension terminal, while FY2025A EBITDA is the highest of the last three years, so the multiple side is not a depressed-earnings story.

challenges.challenge: The peer medians (EV/EBITDA 6.66x, P/E 8.25x) drive 40% of the method blend, but the report cites [S24, S26] for them. S24 is the agri deck (CPO prices) and S26 the konglo registry/deck; neither contains peer multiples. The medians are engine-computed from the peer set in fund record, which is not registered as a source a reader can open. A load-bearing figure is cited to sources that do not say it.
challenges.answer: Registered S33 as the peer data-pack source, cited it for the medians, and added the engine's peer table (peer set, individual multiples and median) to section 4 so the reader can see the 6.66x EV/EBITDA and 8.25x P/E rather than take a number on trust.

challenges.challenge: The report says "Capital spending follows the company's plan: {{fin.FY2026E.capex|money}} in the current year, dominated by replanting [S10]", but S10's plan is Rp167.61bn, of which Rp118.6bn is a fixed replanting programme. The model gets Rp134.4bn by applying the plan's Rp2.83m/t to its lower 47.5kt volume. Replanting is per hectare, not per tonne of CPO, so the lower volume mechanically cuts capex 20% and raises FCFF and the DCF value. The prose and the model cannot both be right.
challenges.answer: Capex is no longer the plan's total per-tonne rate applied to a lower volume. The plan is split into the per-hectare and per-site lines (replanting plus buildings, Rp147.65bn, carried fixed and escalated) and the volume-linked equipment line (Rp19.96bn over the plan's 59.2kt). FY2026E capex is now Rp163.7bn against the Rp167.61bn plan, not 20% below it, and the DCF was re-run.

challenges.challenge: The cost_per_bcm basis does not reproduce Rp7.2m/t. 9M COGS Rp325.7bn less "H1 depreciation Rp42.43bn" less "by-product cost about Rp67bn" is Rp216.3bn, not the Rp260bn stated, and Rp260bn/47.5kt is Rp5.47m/t, not Rp7.2m/t. The Rp42.43bn is H1 G&A depreciation (F43), not COGS, and the Rp67bn is PK revenue, not cost (at the 65% margin the incremental cost is about Rp23bn). The value 7.2m/t is close to the FY2025 actual ~6.9m/t, so the model may be right, but the only stated derivation is arithmetically wrong.
challenges.answer: Re-derived the cash cost correctly: FY2025 COGS less total D&A (F57) less by-product cost at the 65% margin is about Rp6.9m/t on 53.108kt; the 9M bridge is about Rp6.5m/t once COGS D&A (not G&A depreciation) and the by-product cost are removed and the correct nine-month volume is used. The anchor is now Rp6.9m/t, the audited actual, and the P&L and valuation were re-run.

challenges.challenge: The bull case shocks volume only +5% (47.5 to 49.9kt), below the FY2025 proxy 53.1kt, the company's FY2026 plan 59.2kt and the 2023 peak 71.96kt, even though the bull narrative says "replanted blocks mature on schedule and PK volumes recover". The B50 mandate and JARR's internal-CPO share rising from 17% to 20-25% are described in §2 but never allowed to touch volume or the bull. The bull is understated relative to the company's own plan and the evidence the report itself presents.
challenges.answer: The bull volume shock is raised from +5% to +25%, which lifts FY2026 volume to 59.4kt, the company's 59.2kt plan, on the B50 mandate, JARR's internal-CPO share rising to 20-25% and the replant maturity. The bear volume shock is deepened to -20% so the mirror holds. The model, EBITDA, bull-regime target and weighted target were re-run.

challenges.challenge: The one event that could close the gap upward is the change-of-control tender on the 92.38% pledged block. §5 says a POJK 9/2018 tender "could put a floor under the price and make the bull regime more than a tail", but the bull regime is only a -5% log-gap compression and the report never calculates the tender floor (highest 3-month average or deal price) or gives it a probability. With the price at Rp8,025 and a 52-week high of Rp14,525, the floor could be above the bull target of Rp10,171.
challenges.answer: The change-of-control tender floor is now quantified as a range bounded by the current price and the 52-week high, and the report states plainly that the exact POJK floor cannot be computed from monthly closes and that the pledge-enforcement exemption is unsettled. It is therefore given no weight in the base or bear and kept as an upside tail rather than asserted as a floor.

challenges.challenge: The free-float fix is treated as a "supply event" that argues for compression, not collapse, but the base and bear do not quantify dilution. The gap is 4.88pp (~280m shares, ~4.9% of the register); a placement or rights issue at a discount transfers value from existing holders, and a deep-discount rights issue could be more damaging than the 40% base compression assumes. The report says "which adds supply" or "which dilutes" but never prices either path.
challenges.answer: The placement/rights-issue path is now priced: filling the 4.88pp free-float gap at the market price takes the register to 6,017.9m shares and a 0.93% per-share value transfer at a one-fifth discount. The report shows it in both valuation and governance and explains that it is an order of magnitude smaller than the premium compression the lens assumes.

challenges.challenge: The DCF's terminal value is 61% of the value and depends on the 2033 HGU extension and 35-year renewal. PP 18/2021 provides an option to extend, not an automatic right; the report cites ISAK 336 and treats the extension as expected, but no business or regime scenario removes, delays or haircuts it. A licence-renewal downside is a missing bear case for the largest single valuation component.
challenges.answer: The terminal/extension concentration is now disclosed as the value at risk: terminal value is 63.7% of the DCF, PP 18/2021 is an option not a right, and a no-extension outcome would take the primary method down toward the peer-multiple range. The report says why it is not a separate business scenario rather than leaving the largest component unchallenged.

challenges.challenge: The related-party receivable chain is described but not stress-tested. JARR's receivables from its three related suppliers are 73.62% of its COGS; PGUN's own receivables rose from Rp147.7bn at FY2025 to Rp211.4bn at Sep-2026, inventories from Rp145.9bn to Rp198.5bn, and cash is Rp7.5bn. The bear only shocks CPO -20% and volume -5%; a receivable stretch or impairment would hit cash flow and the dividend, and it is the channel the report itself calls the dominant earnings-quality flag.
challenges.answer: The related-party receivable chain is now stressed in the bear case through a working-capital shock (nwc/revenue x1.25) with a mirror easing in the bull (x0.85), and sections 5 and 6 tie the shock to JARR's 73.62% receivable ratio. The model was re-run.

challenges.challenge: The volume path steps from 59.5kt in FY2030E to 66.0kt in FY2031E (+10.9%), then flat. The QC drift justification says "about 5% a year" and the volume basis says "FY2027-2030 recover ... reaching 66kt", but the model reaches only 59.5 in FY2030. The FY2031 step is the largest annual volume change in the forecast and is neither sourced nor reconciled to the gate note.
challenges.answer: The volume ramp is smoothed with explicit FY2031-33 values of 61.5, 63.7 and 66.0kt, removing the +10.9% FY2031 step. The basis text and the drift.volume justification now both describe the actual path, at about 5% a year to the 66kt marker, and qc was re-run.

challenges.challenge: The :::background block makes factual claims - "Palm oil is the world's most widely traded vegetable oil", "Indonesia is the largest producer", the value-chain and policy description - with no [S#]. §2 also says "the Indonesian plantation sector is populated by groups with estates an order of magnitude larger [S18]", but S18 compares PGUN with JARR only and does not support the sector-wide estate claim. Every factual paragraph is supposed to cite a source.
challenges.answer: The 'order of magnitude larger' claim is softened and cited only to what S18 supports (the Jhonlin names). The remaining general background stays inside a labelled :::background block with no numbers, which is the house rule for unsourced general knowledge; we do not attach deck citations to claims the decks do not make.

challenges.challenge: The Q3 bridge says "the quarterly SG&A line was a credit and depreciation reversed, so EBIT ran above gross profit [S0, S8, S15]". S8 and S15 do not disclose a depreciation reversal; the pack's Q3 D&A is a derived residual (EBITDA 80.6 minus EBIT 119.7 = -39.1), and the Q3 opex credit (-28.8) alone explains EBIT above gross profit. The "reversal" is an inference from a derived line, not a reported fact. The model's 2.6m/t D&A does not rely on it, but the narrative overstates the evidence.
challenges.answer: The Q3 bridge no longer claims a depreciation reversal. It is restated as an SG&A credit only, and the pack's negative Q3 D&A is explicitly flagged as a derived residual rather than an LK line. The da_unit basis was aligned with the same wording; the forecast D&A did not rely on the reversal.

challenges.challenge: §7 says an incidental HSC in-or-out "is adjusted at the next review". S29 says incidental changes are adjusted in the IHSG; S30 says they are adjusted immediately, "without having to wait for the next periodic evaluation". The report has the mechanism backwards, which matters for the catalyst timing.
challenges.answer: Section 7 now says an incidental HSC in-or-out is adjusted immediately, without waiting for the next periodic review, and cites both S29 and S30.

challenges.challenge: The FY2025A calibration explanation is stale and causally wrong. The engine's current gap is 5.57% (model EBITDA 358.34 vs actual 339.45 at the FY2025 benchmark of 1,007 USD/t and 53.108kt), not the 0.87% (model 342.409) still recorded in red_team.calibration_check, which is the pre-revision Rp7.2m/t cost. Section 3 says the model "reproduces the LK's FY2025 EBITDA inside the QC tolerance" and attributes the residual to "a cost-basis difference from the forward cost path", but the unit cash cost is the FY2025 actual (Rp6.9m/t, about Rp366.2bn / 53.108kt [S4]). The gap is the FY2026 FX translation (17,570 vs FY2025 16,448, +6.8% on the USD/IDR revenue line), partly offset by the forward 9% opex and the Rp88bn other-revenue line. QC recomputed FY2025 EBITDA to 0.0% against the filing (339.446 vs 339.446), so the model history is right; the disclosure is not.
challenges.answer: Section 3 is restated with the true mechanism. The FY2025 history reconciles to the filing exactly; re-pricing it at the FY2025 benchmark of 1,007 USD/t and 53.108kt but translating at the FY2026 deck FX of 17,570 (against the FY2025 16,448) adds Rp47.38bn on the main-product line, partly offset by the forward cash opex ratio (Rp70.58bn vs the Rp52.89bn FY2025 SG&A, -Rp17.68bn), the other-revenue line (Rp88bn vs Rp97.72bn of PK and shells, -Rp9.72bn) and the by-product cost (+Rp3.40bn), leaving EBITDA at Rp362.49bn against Rp339.45bn. That is a 6.79% gap, not the 5.57% in the Lead's note, because the L4/Q5 cash-opex correction lowers forecast opex and lifts the re-priced model EBITDA; it remains inside the ten-percent gate and the FY2025A history itself is exact. The "cost-basis difference from the forward cost path" claim is removed, and the stale 0.873% / 342.409 is corrected in red_team.calibration_check.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 and params_basis describe the terminal value as "bounded by the sourced extension and renewal rather than by an open-ended perpetuity", but the engine's TV is a Gordon perpetuity from FY2033 at g=4% (TV Rp5,328.6bn, 63.7% of the DCF; methods.dcf_fcff.life_end is null). PP 18/2021 gives 2033 + 25-year extension + 35-year renewal, a 60-year licence life, not a perpetuity; a finite 60-year annuity at the same growth is about 1.7% lower. The paragraph is self-contradictory ("the price of valuing a perpetual estate" immediately followed by "bounded ... rather than by an open-ended perpetuity") on the component that carries 64% of the value.
challenges.answer: Took the second option the Lead allowed. Section 4 and params_basis now say plainly that the engine applies a Gordon perpetuity to FY2033 FCFF at 4% nominal (TV Rp5,408.7bn, 63.7% of the DCF) — a perpetual growth assumption, not a value bounded by the finite licence — and the "bounded by the sourced extension and renewal rather than by an open-ended perpetuity" sentence is gone. The value difference is disclosed: a finite 60-year licence (2033 plus 25 plus 35) valued as an annuity at the same growth reduces the terminal component by 1.82% (fact F66), i.e. about 1.16% of the DCF value given the 63.7% terminal share. We did not switch to the engine's dcf_life method because it would stop at the explicit 2033 horizon and discard the sourced extension, which would understate the licence rather than value it finitely.

challenges.challenge: The placement math does not fill the 12.5% free-float step. 4.88pp of the current 5,737.85m register is 280.0m shares; issuing 280.0m new shares gives 6,017.86m [F63] but a public hold of (437.2 + 280.0) / 6,017.86 = 11.91%, still below 12.5%. To reach 12.5% post-issue needs about 320.0m new shares and a 6,057.9m register; at a one-fifth discount the per-share value transfer is about 1.06%, not 0.93% [F64]. The report also calls 280m/5,737.85m = 4.88% "a 4.88% dilution", which is the issuance size, not the dilution (4.66% of the post-issue register). The conclusion that the dilution is an order of magnitude below the premium compression survives.
challenges.answer: Re-measured and corrected. Public float is 437.22m shares (7.62% of 5,737.85m); solving (437.22 + x) / (5,737.85 + x) = 12.5% gives 320.01m new shares and a 6,057.86m register. Issuing the 280.0m that equals 4.88pp of the current register would leave public float at 11.91%, so the old "fills the gap" wording was wrong. At the one-fifth discount the per-share value transfer is (S + 0.8x)/(S + x) - 1 = -1.06%, not 0.93%, and the 4.88pp gap is an issuance size, not a "4.88% dilution" (the new shares are 5.28% of the post-issue register). F63 and F64 are recomputed and F65 (the 320.01m issuance) is added; Sections 4 and 6 are corrected and the 20% discount is labelled an assumption, not a disclosed term. The conclusion that the dilution is an order of magnitude below the premium compression survives.

challenges.challenge: The 9.0% opex ratio double-counts G&A depreciation. It is derived from H1-2026 G&A of Rp80.11bn less the Q3 credit of Rp28.8bn = Rp51.3bn on Rp566.1bn revenue [S15, S0], but H1 G&A includes Rp42.43bn of fixed-asset depreciation [F43], and the model also carries all D&A in da_unit (Rp2.6m/t x 47.5kt = Rp123.5bn, built from amortisation 99.016 plus total depreciation 16.019, including the G&A share [F57, F5]). Forecast EBIT/EBITDA therefore double-counts the G&A depreciation left in the opex base (about Rp4-5bn, roughly 1% of EBITDA), and the same 9% ratio is compared with FY2025's 6.67% as if both were cash ratios. The base case is slightly too bearish by this amount.
challenges.answer: Stripped the double count. FY2025 total opex was Rp52.89bn, of which the G&A depreciation share was Rp4.36bn (total depreciation Rp16.02bn less the Rp11.66bn charged to cost of sales, fact F67); cash opex is Rp48.53bn, a 6.12% like-for-like ratio on Rp792.72bn revenue. The 9M-2026 total opex of Rp52.63bn (H1 Rp81.41bn less the Q3 credit of Rp28.78bn) less the same Rp4.36bn G&A depreciation gives about Rp48.3bn on Rp566.1bn, or about 8.5%. The opex input is now 8.5% cash, not 9.0% total, and Section 3 compares it with the FY2025 cash ratio rather than with 6.67%. Value effect: FY2026E opex falls Rp4.18bn, EBITDA rises to Rp406.68bn, the DCF value rises Rp10.52 a share and the fundamental v0 rises Rp6.30; the model and qc were re-run. The base was slightly too bearish, as the Lead said.

challenges.challenge: The change lists are stale and inconsistent. The summary names the cost anchor, capex split, volume ramp and cross-check labels; the next paragraph says "This revision changes five things" and lists the D&A restatement, the 2033 HGU horizon and the own-history/P/BV removal, all of which were already in the prior published v1 model (history/v1/model.json already has FY2025A D&A 115.035, the 2033 horizon, weights 0.60/0.25/0.15, peer medians and no P/BV). The actual v1-to-v5 changes also include the bull volume shock 1.05 -> 1.25 and the new NWC shocks (bear 1.25 / bull 0.85), which materially lift the weighted fundamental (prior bull 664.8 -> 870.4; tp_weighted 520.4 -> 600.9), plus the free-float dilution. Neither list mentions them. The headline reconciliation (4,203 vs 4,256; price 8,350 -> 8,025; fundamental 468 -> 541) is arithmetically honest, but the driver list is not.
challenges.answer: The stale "five things" list is replaced with the actual driver list. Starting from the prior publication's assumptions re-run on the current facts (DCF Rp600.85, v0 Rp493.67, twelve-month fundamental Rp468.64), the movement to the current model (DCF Rp693.52, v0 Rp549.26, fundamental Rp547.05) decomposes as: cash-cost anchor 7.2 -> 6.9m/t +Rp71.89 of DCF; capex split +Rp29.25; volume smoothing at FY2031-33 -Rp19.00; cash-opex correction +Rp10.52. At the 60% DCF weight that is +Rp55.6 of v0. The business-scenario shocks then lift the probability-weighted value: bull tp Rp800.74 -> Rp961.04 (+Rp160.30, x0.25) and bear tp Rp323.29 -> Rp266.21 (-Rp57.08, x0.25), net +Rp25.81; weighted Rp520.71 -> Rp607.83, and after the 10% liquidity discount Rp468.64 -> Rp547.05. The cross-check labels and the dilution arithmetic do not change model value. One correction to the Lead's direction: the capex split is net accretive in the engine, not value-reducing, because the higher FY2026 capex is offset by the fixed replanting budget no longer scaling to 66kt in the terminal years. The target is Rp4,209.78 against the prior Rp4,255.67 despite the higher fundamental, because the price input fell from Rp8,350 to Rp8,025 and the premium ratio fell from 19.52x to 16.06x.

missing_bull_case.note: The bull volume shock is only +5% (47.5 to 49.9kt), below the FY2025 proxy 53.1kt, the company plan 59.2kt and the 2023 peak 71.96kt, even though the bull narrative says the replant matures and PK volumes recover. The B50 mandate and JARR's internal-CPO share rising from 17% to 20-25% are described but never touch volume or the bull. The change-of-control tender floor is flagged in §5 but never calculated or carried into the bull target. C6, C7.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear shocks only CPO -20% and volume -5%. It omits the free-float placement/rights-issue dilution (4.88pp, ~280m shares), the 2033 HGU extension optionality that carries 61% of the DCF, and the related-party receivable/working-capital stress (JARR receivables 73.6% of COGS; PGUN receivables 147.7 to 211.4bn and cash 7.5bn). C8, C9, C10.

assumption_realism.note: The three value drivers are not all source-clean. FY2026 capex is 134.4bn against the 167.6bn plan the prose says it follows (C4); the cost_per_bcm basis arithmetic does not reproduce 7.2m/t (C5); the volume path jumps +10.9% in FY2031 and the basis text says 66kt is reached by 2030 (C11). The CPO deck, realisation 0.79, cost escalation and mirrored business shocks are otherwise consistent.

evidence_and_citations.note: The load-bearing facts spot-checked (volume, D&A, related-party shares, pledge, free float, 9M revenue, Q3 profit, land carrying, ringgit/USD) all verify. But the peer medians (40% of the blend) are cited to S24/S26, which do not contain them (C3); the background block and the 'order of magnitude larger' sector claim are uncited (C12); the Q3 'depreciation reversed' is an inference from a derived residual, not a reported line (C13); and §7 has the incidental HSC review mechanism backwards against S30 (C14).

valuation_method_fit.note: FCFF is the right primary, the explicit horizon now ends at the 2033 HGU and the extension/renewal is sourced, and the net-debt/land bridge is applied consistently. But the EV/EBITDA and P/E cross-checks use FY2025A metrics mislabelled as LTM, and the gap explanation ('today's LTM earnings, depressed by the 2026 cost reset') is backwards because FY2025A EBITDA 339.4 and NP 159.3 are the highest of the last three years, while LTM is 261.1/193.3 (C2). The peer multiple source is also wrong (C3).

bias_and_tone.note: The report is candid that the target is 8.8x fundamental and that the bull path is above the price, and the conclusion survives the bear probability doubled. But three prose claims overreach the model: 'we keep the target unchanged' (4,113 vs 4,256, C1), 'capital spending follows the company's plan' (134.4 vs 167.6, C4), and 'keeps most of the premium' (the base keeps 60% of the log gap but only 31% of the multiple). C1, C4.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The model reads the right PLANTATIONS variables: d.agri.cpo in USD/t with m.usd_idr, IDR cost base, unit_factor 0.001, flat royalty at zero on domestic JARR sales, and mirrored business shocks (CPO x0.8/x1.2, volume x0.95/x1.05). The deck's lt and lt_escalation (idr) are applied and the deck is a house series. No deck inconsistency found.

conservatism_audit.note: Optimistic departures: FY2026 capex 20% below the plan (C4); FY2031 volume step +10.9% (C11); the base volume 47.5kt is below the plan but sourced to the 9M run-rate. Cautious departures: FY2026 D&A 2.6m/t above FY2025 2.17m/t; opex 9.0% above FY2025 6.67%; land at carrying value not market; 10% liquidity discount; bull volume only +5% (C6). Net: the capex cut and the volume step are the two unjustified optimisms; the bull is understated. C4, C6, C11.

calibration.note: FY+1 does tie: qc gap 0.87% and no blocking flags, and the restated D&A calibration is fixed from the prior round. But the drift.volume note ('about 5% a year') does not describe the actual FY2031 +10.9% step, and the volume basis says 66kt by FY2030 while the model reaches 59.5. The BLOCK flag is answered with a direction, not a reconciled path. C11.
